boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Randolph-Macon rituals, gatherings, and markers of Yellow Jacket life.

cards.title: Follow The Game
cards.subtitle: Randolph-Macon vs. Hampden-Sydney football
cards.notes: See the annual Randolph-Macon–Hampden-Sydney football matchup and follow College athletics for the next scheduled contest.
cards.short_summary: RMC’s long-running football rivalry is known simply as “The Game.”
cards.evidence_claim: Randolph-Macon identifies The Game as its football series with Hampden-Sydney, first played in 1893 and described as the oldest small-college rivalry in the South.
cards.source_title: 10 R-MC Traditions To Look Forward To
cards.access_notes: Event timing and attendance details vary by season; consult Randolph-Macon athletics before visiting.

cards.title: Read the Alumni Walkway
cards.subtitle: Campus red-brick alumni path
cards.notes: Walk the red-brick path through campus and look down for alumni names incorporated into this lasting campus marker.
cards.short_summary: A campus walkway records generations of Randolph-Macon alumni in brick.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says the Janet Harvey Trivette ’78 Alumni Walkway was dedicated in 2008 and contains names of RMC alumni back through the early 1950s.
cards.source_title: 10 R-MC Traditions To Look Forward To
cards.access_notes: Use normal campus visitor access practices; the College page does not state public-access conditions.

cards.title: Join Macon a Difference Day
cards.subtitle: Annual spring service tradition in Ashland
cards.notes: Watch Student Life announcements for spring volunteer registration, then take on a community project with fellow Yellow Jackets.
cards.short_summary: Students gather for hands-on service projects benefiting Ashland neighbors.
cards.evidence_claim: Randolph-Macon describes Macon a Difference Day as an annual spring service tradition that brings students together for projects around Ashland.
cards.source_title: 10 R-MC Traditions To Look Forward To
cards.access_notes: Projects and sign-up details vary annually; participate through College-organized volunteer information.

cards.title: Volunteer at The Big Event
cards.subtitle: Fall service day around Ashland
cards.notes: Look for the fall service-day sign-up and choose a hands-on project such as painting, construction, or gardening as assigned.
cards.short_summary: The Big Event is RMC’s fall counterpart to its spring community-service day.
cards.evidence_claim: Randolph-Macon identifies The Big Event as a fall service day, paired with Macon a Difference Day, for hands-on projects serving Ashland residents.
cards.source_title: 10 R-MC Traditions To Look Forward To
cards.access_notes: Project locations, eligibility, and sign-up details vary annually; follow College volunteer guidance.

cards.title: Mark spring at Fountain Turn On
cards.subtitle: Brown Fountain Plaza
cards.notes: Gather at Brown Fountain Plaza when the College announces the seasonal fountain switch-on, then stay for the shared program.
cards.short_summary: The return of Brown Fountain signals Randolph-Macon’s unofficial start of spring.
cards.evidence_claim: The College calls Fountain Turn On its unofficial rite of spring, held at Brown Fountain Plaza when the fountain is switched back on.
cards.source_title: 10 R-MC Traditions To Look Forward To
cards.access_notes: Seasonal date and program details are announced by the College; outdoor conditions may affect the event.

cards.title: Sign into the RMC community
cards.subtitle: Entering-student academic-integrity ceremony
cards.notes: As an entering student, follow Welcome Week instructions and add your name to the Matriculation record as directed.
cards.short_summary: New Yellow Jackets formally enter RMC through a signed matriculation tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Randolph-Macon says entering students continue to add their names to the Matriculation roster, following generations who signed the official book.
cards.source_title: 10 R-MC Traditions To Look Forward To
cards.access_notes: For entering students; ceremony instructions and timing are provided through the College’s orientation program.

cards.title: Share Estes Thanksgiving
cards.subtitle: Estes Dining Hall before holiday break
cards.notes: Check the dining calendar before Thanksgiving break and plan a meal with friends at Estes during the special holiday service.
cards.short_summary: Estes Dining Hall hosts a yearly Thanksgiving meal before students leave for break.
cards.evidence_claim: The College describes Estes Thanksgiving as an annual special Thanksgiving meal at Estes Dining Hall before the holiday break.
cards.source_title: 10 R-MC Traditions To Look Forward To
cards.access_notes: Dining access and the exact menu are determined by current dining operations.

cards.title: Catch Camptown
cards.subtitle: Annual spring concert and carnival
cards.notes: Use the Camptown page for the current April schedule, then attend the College concert or carnival activities as eligible.
cards.short_summary: Since 1978, Camptown has been RMC’s spring music-and-amusements tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Randolph-Macon says Camptown has been an annual spring tradition since 1978 and its 2026 event is scheduled for April 17–18.
cards.access_notes: The College lists Camptown 2026 for April 17–18; specific activity access and ticketing may vary.

cards.title: Receive your class ring
cards.subtitle: Senior tradition during Family Weekend
cards.notes: Eligible seniors can watch Family Weekend communications for ring ordering and ceremony details, then attend with invited guests.
cards.short_summary: Seniors formally receive class rings during a Family Weekend ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Randolph-Macon states that seniors gather with loved ones during Family Weekend to formally accept their class rings at Ring Ceremony.
cards.source_title: 10 R-MC Traditions To Look Forward To
cards.access_notes: Intended for seniors and their invited guests; ring ordering and ceremony arrangements are set by the College.

cards.title: Sign the Four-Year Degree Guarantee
cards.subtitle: Entering-student commitment ritual
cards.notes: During entry programming, review the guarantee requirements with family and advisers before signing the College’s agreement.
cards.short_summary: New students formally sign RMC’s four-year completion guarantee.
cards.evidence_claim: Randolph-Macon identifies signing its Four-Year Degree Guarantee as a traditional part of an entering student’s experience.
cards.source_title: 10 R-MC Traditions To Look Forward To
cards.access_notes: For entering students; review the current guarantee terms and academic-advising requirements with the College.
